headline: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham promised new law to curb non-compete clauses that stop workers moving to rival firms.
score_reason: Kept at 5: an on-record government promise, but the scope is undecided and nothing is law yet.
importance_line: Around 5 million UK workers are covered by such clauses, according to research the government cites, and startups including AI firms stand to hire more easily, but the scope will not be known until the Budget on 28 October and employers warn against sweeping changes.
summary: The BBC reports that UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham promised in a speech in Manchester to legislate so that non-compete clauses, which limit where staff can work after leaving a job, are “no longer a barrier” to hiring, but did not say how far the limits would go. Details are expected with the Budget on 28 October, and an employers' recruitment body warns against sweeping changes.
notes: Bloomberg original (403) not readable; BBC text read, plus Tech.eu for the startup campaign (ElevenLabs, Synthesia). BBC credits Politico and the Financial Times for the first report of the plan; the BBC itself reports the speech.
